gloss: riding on someone's shoulders; shoulder ride

definitions.gloss: riding on someone's shoulders; shoulder ride; piggyback on shoulders
definitions.explanation: Carrying a person (usually a child) on one's shoulders, with their legs hanging down on either side of the carrier's neck. A common sight at festivals, parades, and family outings.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}に{肩車|かたぐるま}をしてもらった。
examples.english: My father gave me a shoulder ride.

examples.japanese: {花火|はなび}{大会|たいかい}で{子供|こども}を{肩車|かたぐるま}した。
examples.english: I carried my child on my shoulders at the fireworks festival.

examples.japanese: {人混|ひとご}みで{前|まえ}が{見|み}えないので、{肩車|かたぐるま}をして{見|み}せてあげた。
examples.english: Since they couldn't see past the crowd, I put them on my shoulders so they could see.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
Used with する: {肩車|かたぐるま}する (to give a shoulder ride) or {肩車|かたぐるま}をする. The person being carried is not usually the subject — the carrier performs the action.

USAGE:
{肩車|かたぐるま} is a warm, nostalgic word associated with childhood memories. It literally combines {肩|かた} (shoulder) and {車|くるま} (vehicle), suggesting the shoulders as a kind of vehicle for the child.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {肩車|かたぐるま}をする (to give a shoulder ride)
- {肩車|かたぐるま}をしてもらう (to get a shoulder ride)
- {子供|こども}を{肩車|かたぐるま}する (to carry a child on one's shoulders)
